articles.title: NHS Staff at Rochdale Infirmary to Strike Over Overtime Pay Dispute
articles.excerpt: More than 350 staff at Rochdale Infirmary and three other Greater Manchester hospitals will strike for three days next week due to a dispute over overtime payments, according to UNISON.
articles.content_html:
More than 350 employees of the Northern Care Alliance Foundation Trust (NCA), including nurses and clinical support workers at Rochdale Infirmary, will strike for three days next week. The strike is scheduled for Monday 24th, Wednesday 26th, and Friday 28th August, as part of an ongoing dispute regarding overtime payments.

The dispute arises from the NCA's use of NHS Professionals (NHSP) to manage overtime, which has reportedly led to staff earning less than their usual pay rates. UNISON claims that some staff are missing out on more than £80 per shift due to this arrangement, which contradicts their contractual entitlements to time-and-a-half pay when covering staff shortages.

Kevin Dolan, UNISON's North West regional organiser, expressed frustration over the situation, stating that a resolution offer was made by NCA management but subsequently withdrawn before discussions could take place. He emphasised that staff are simply asking for what they are contractually owed and accused NCA leadership of lacking commitment to resolving the issue.

In addition to the strikes, staff from all four affected hospitals, including Rochdale Infirmary, Royal Oldham Hospital, Fairfield Hospital in Bury, and Salford Royal Hospital, will gather in Salford on Wednesday 26th August for a unified day of protest.

articles.title: Plans for 450 New Homes on Former Green Belt Land in Bamford
articles.excerpt: Developers are moving forward with plans to build hundreds of homes on former green belt land in Bamford, following the removal of its protected status in 2024.
articles.content_html:
Hundreds of new homes are set to be built on former green belt land in Bamford, Rochdale, as developers ramp up plans following the area's removal from protected status. The site, which spans a vast area of grassland, has been earmarked for 450 houses as part of the Greater Manchester-wide Places for Everyone plan adopted in 2024.

Northstone, a subsidiary of The Peel Group, is currently preparing a hybrid planning application for 350 homes. This development will be split across two sites on the western edge of the land off Norden Road, with 140 homes planned for the southern plot in phase one and a further 210 homes for the northern plot in phase two. The proposed development aims to include high-quality, energy-efficient homes, new cycle and walking routes, two children's play areas, and a green linear park.

The developers are consulting with local residents about their proposals and expect to submit a planning application to Rochdale Council by the end of 2026. Planning documents indicate that 20 per cent of the new homes will be affordable, aimed at those who cannot afford to buy or rent on the open market. The plans also include improvements to existing sports pitches on the site.

Other developers, including Wain Homes and McCarthy and Stone, have already submitted planning applications for their respective schemes, although Wain Homes' application has faced delays due to concerns over drainage issues raised by the council's planning committee. Councillor Tom Besford expressed concerns about the lack of an overall masterplan for the area, fearing that piecemeal development could undermine the benefits intended for the community.

This initiative follows the removal of the area from the green belt as part of the Greater Manchester-wide Places for Everyone plan, adopted in 2024. The local community has been anticipating the construction of new housing, with a total of 450 homes initially earmarked for the site.

articles.title: Rochdale Commemorates Comedian Jimmy Cricket Ahead of Funeral
articles.excerpt: Rochdale will pay tribute to comedian Jimmy Cricket, who passed away on August 3, with a public viewing at St Patrick’s Catholic Church before his funeral at Salford Cathedral.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale will have the opportunity to remember legendary comedian Jimmy Cricket ahead of his funeral next week. Jimmy Cricket, known for his clean humour and catchphrase 'And there’s more', died on August 3 at the age of 80 after a short illness, surrounded by family.

His body will lie in state at St Patrick’s Catholic Church in Rochdale on Thursday, August 20, from 3pm to 5pm for those wishing to pay their respects. Following this, a vigil mass will take place at Salford Cathedral at 7pm, marking the reception of his body.

The funeral service is scheduled for 1.30pm on Friday, August 21, at Salford Cathedral. Mourners are encouraged to wear bow ties, which, along with his iconic Wellington boots, became Jimmy’s trademark attire.

Jimmy Cricket was a prominent figure in the comedy scene during the 1970s and was a dedicated supporter of local charities and causes in Rochdale. His contributions to the community and his legacy in comedy will be fondly remembered by many.
